revision_reason: Stage A used a linear learning-rate scheduler parameterized for max_steps=200 and the optimizer learning rate reached zero at step 200. Direct checkpoint continuation would therefore not constitute a clean controlled horizon extension.
objective: Measure training adequacy along one common 500-step optimization trajectory and determine whether performance continues improving beyond 200 steps.

stage_a_role.comparison_role: External reference only. Stage A step 200 and Stage B step 200 are not expected to be numerically identical because their linear schedulers are parameterized by different total budgets.

horizon_protocol.optional_extension_rule: Do not extend automatically. Reassess only if step 500 remains the best candidate and the boundary signal indicates material continued improvement.

interpretation_protocol.valid_internal_comparison: Compare Stage B checkpoints 200, 300, 400, and 500 because they belong to the same model initialization, dataset, optimizer configuration, and 500-step learning-rate schedule.
interpretation_protocol.invalid_equivalence: Do not interpret Stage A step 200 and Stage B step 200 as identical training states.
interpretation_protocol.primary_question: Does Optimization Dev performance continue improving after the 200-step observation point under a common longer training trajectory?
